subject: Commercial path & procurement readiness — Celeratek (PO vs card / marketplace)
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Turner <eliot.turner@celeratek.com>; Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps — procurement & commercial path options

Thanks again for walking through the use case today, Eliot — appreciated the context on inference volume and the pilot goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on procurement readiness and commercial paths that map to your purchasing rules.

TL;DR: Based on the pilot profile you shared (burst to 800 rps for short spikes, steady 50k tokens/day, strict data isolation for some workloads) the two routes that fit your procurement and finance preferences are: (A) Hosted API with invoice/PO billing (on-demand) for initial pilot + marketplace listing to simplify procurement; or (B) Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) with optional private deployment later for regulated workloads.

Recap items from call:
- Pilot scope: inference for customer-facing summary feature (English only) + internal batch embedding job for search re-ranking.
- Sequence/latency: 90% requests under 1s target, occasional spikes tolerated up to 3s.
- Procurement: "PO-first" for any vendor >$25k annually; card allowed for low-dollar pilots. Procurement will need vendor packet, SOC2 evidence, and W9.
- Marketplace: you asked whether a cloud marketplace purchase would cut the PO step — potentially yes, depending on procurement's vendor policy.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a concise vendor packet (SOC2 summary, pricing matrix, T&Cs) for procurement to review — Monica will attach SOC2 summary and a starter SOW.
2) You’ll confirm whether procurement prefers: PO to Redwood (monthly invoice) OR procurement via Cloud Marketplace (single-vendor billing).
3) If PO path, we’ll draft a simple commercial term: 3-month pilot on hosted on-demand, capped spend $20k, with optional upgrade to Dedicated commit if you hit forecasted throughput.
4) If marketplace path, we’ll identify which marketplace (Jacob from Cloud Marketplace is on this thread) and map billing timing and invoice needs.

Ask: Can you loop in the procurement contact (procurement@celeratek.com) with a target review date? If you can share the specific vendor packet requirements (insurance, W9, PO contact), we’ll prioritize those docs.

Attachments referenced: vendor_packet_Celeratek.pdf (attached), redwood_pricing_v2.xlsx (pricing scenarios).

Thanks — I’ll be standing by to coordinate the packet and next steps.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129

From: Eliot Turner <eliot.turner@celeratek.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Celeratek Procurement <procurement@celeratek.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — procurement & commercial path options

Thanks, Sergio — that captures it. A few clarifications from procurement (looping them in):

- Procurement note (Procurement contact): For anything above $25k/year we require a PO and a signed vendor agreement. For pilots under $5k we can use a corporate card.
- Marketplace: We prefer marketplace purchases when available since billing/tax handling is simplified, but product availability and SKUs must match our internal chart of accounts. If Redwood is on the AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace with a matching SKU for a pilot bundle, procurement can approve faster.
- Required docs: vendor packet (W9, primary contact, insurance), SOC2 attestation summary, pricing breakdown.

Timeline: Procurement can provide an initial review within 5 business days after we receive the packet. Our legal team will need to review terms if we go the direct PO + vendor agreement route.

For the pilot we’d like to start with hosted on-demand (card or PO depending on final amount) but reserve the option to move to Dedicated commits if utilization grows. Also open to a marketplace path if the SKU and term map cleanly.

I’ll ask procurement to confirm specific marketplace preference (AWS vs Azure) by EOD Friday.

—
Eliot Turner
Head of Platform, Celeratek
eliot.turner@celeratek.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Eliot Turner <eliot.turner@celeratek.com>, Celeratek Procurement <procurement@celeratek.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Next: Proposed commercial paths and matching docs (short summary)

Appreciate the quick clarity, Eliot. Short commercial mapping to help procurement choose:

Option A — Hosted (on-demand) + invoice/PO
- How it maps to procurement: Redwood can accept PO invoicing (net 30/45) for billed usage.
- Best for: fast pilot, minimal ops, no infra commitments.
- Pricing mechanics: per-token on-demand, with a pilot spend cap to control finance exposure.
- Docs needed: W9, SOC2 summary, vendor packet.

Option B — Hosted marketplace SKU
- How it maps: Purchase via AWS/Azure marketplace (if Redwood listing exists with SKU matching usage). Procurement benefits: single invoice, simpler tax/treatment, and sometimes faster approvals.
- Caveat: Marketplace SKUs sometimes lack flexibility on custom billing cadence or immediate overage protection.

Option C — Dedicated (reserved capacity) commit
- How it maps: Monthly committed spend (minimum term) billed by PO or contract. Best when you need predictable throughput and data isolation. Can include a private deployment later for regulated workloads.
- Procurement impact: larger initial commitment triggers full legal review; may require finance sign-off and procurement approval cycles.

Recommendation for pilot: Start with Option A (hosted on-demand) with a purchase method based on expected spend: card if <$5k, PO if >$5k and < $25k (or card if procurement allows), and explicit commit discussion only if forecasted 3-month usage looks above $25k. We can include an explicit upgrade path to Dedicated with credits for pilot spend toward commit.

I’ve attached the vendor packet and a pricing workbook that lays out example scenarios vs spend. Monica — can you attach the SOC2 summary and a one-page SOW draft?

—
Sergio

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Eliot Turner <eliot.turner@celeratek.com>, Celeratek Procurement <procurement@celeratek.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next: Proposed commercial paths and matching docs (short summary)

Adding the SOC2 summary and starter SOW as requested. A couple of technical clarifications for procurement to consider in the SOW (so finance/legal don't have to chase later):

- Data residency: we can do hosted with customer-specific data partitioning in our hosted environment, or full Private (VPC) for stricter isolation — note that Private has longer lead time and may incur infra setup fees.
- SLA: baseline SLO for pilot: 99.5% uptime, P95 latency targets per model. Higher SLAs available under Dedicated with custom support add-on.
- Support levels: pilot includes standard support and onboarding; Dedicated includes a higher support tier and access to runbooks.

Attachments included: SOC2-summary-2025.pdf, draft_SOW_Celeratek.docx

—
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sergio / Monica — thanks for the packet. Procurement has reviewed the vendor packet and SOC2 summary. A couple of items we need to proceed with a PO: 

1) Completed W9 and primary billing contact (please provide).
2) Sample invoice template showing net-30 terms.
3) Confirmation that pilot can be capped at $20k total spend and that we’ll receive usage reports weekly.

Marketplace update: We prefer AWS Marketplace if Redwood has an appropriate pilot SKU. If you can confirm SKU availability and whether marketplace purchases allow us to apply internal accounting codes, that would be ideal — otherwise we'll proceed with PO.

Tentative timeline: If we receive the above within 3 business days, procurement can issue a PO within 5 business days after that. Please send the missing items to procurement@celeratek.com.

—
Celeratek Procurement Team
